readers-of-basra.title: The Readers of Basra: Quranic Recitation in the Pre-Canonical Period Based on Manuscript Evidence
readers-of-basra.access: Article manuscript in the local research library; publication details to verify

notes.summary: Van Putten’s translation presents al-Dānī’s entry for Abū ʿAmr within the seven-reader system and documents the reader and the two transmitters associated with this account.
notes.scope: A translation and commentary on al-Dānī’s account; it describes that source’s presentation.

notes.summary: Van Putten argues that early references to al-Dūrī could represent a broader Iraqi community of transmitters, while the later two-transmitter presentation narrowed that history into the familiar al-Dūrī/al-Sūsī pairing.
notes.scope: The article’s historical interpretation; it should be read alongside the specific transmission records rather than as a replacement for them.

notes.summary: Van Putten compares vocalized Qur’an manuscripts and argues that a group can be associated with Basra and related to known canonical and non-canonical Basran traditions.
notes.locator: pp. 1–2; manuscript comparisons in the article
notes.scope: Manuscript evidence for a regional reading environment, not a direct isnād for Abū ʿAmr.

notes.entity: Basran reading traditions, including canonical and non-canonical traditions
notes.summary: This manuscript study treats Basra’s early reading landscape as a group of related traditions rather than a single uniform reading. It offers context for studying Yaʿqūb as a Basran reader, but does not establish a manuscript as Yaʿqūb’s own reading.
notes.scope: Regional manuscript context only; the article’s manuscript analysis should not be attributed directly to Yaʿqūb.
